questions.stem: The pitch of a screw gauge is $1 \mathrm{mm}$ and there are $100$ divisions on the circular scale. When nothing is put in between the jaws, the zero of the circular scale lies $4$ divisions below the reference line. When a wire is placed between the jaws, the main scale reads $2 \mathrm{mm}$ and circular scale reads $46$ divisions. The measured diameter of the wire in millimeters is $2.x$. The value of $x$ is:
questions.solution:
Least count $\text{LC} = \frac{\text{Pitch}}{\text{Number of divisions}} = \frac{1 \mathrm{mm}}{100} = 0.01 \mathrm{mm}$.
Since the zero of the circular scale lies $4$ divisions below the reference line, there is a positive zero error:
$\text{Zero error} = +4 \times 0.01 = +0.04 \mathrm{mm}$.
Observed reading = $\text{Main Scale Reading} + (\text{Circular Scale Reading} \times \text{LC})$
$= 2 \mathrm{mm} + (46 \times 0.01 \mathrm{mm}) = 2.46 \mathrm{mm}$.
Corrected reading = Observed reading - Zero error = $2.46 - 0.04 = 2.42 \mathrm{mm}$.
Comparing with $2.x$, we get $x = 42$.

questions.stem:
The pitch of a screw gauge is $1
\mathrm{mm}$ and there are $100$ divisions on the circular scale. When nothing is put in between the jaws, the zero of the circular scale lies $4$ divisions below the reference line. When a wire is placed between the jaws, the main scale reads $2
\mathrm{mm}$ and the circular scale reads $45$ divisions. The correct diameter of the wire is $x \times 10^{-2}
\mathrm{mm}$. The value of $x$ is:
questions.solution:
Least count $\text{LC} = \text{pitch}/\text{divisions} = 1
\mathrm{mm}/100 = 0.01
\mathrm{mm}$.
Zero error: since zero lies $4$ divisions below, the error is positive, $\text{Zero Error} = +4 \times 0.01
\mathrm{mm} = +0.04
\mathrm{mm}$.
Measured reading $= \text{MSR} + \text{CSR} \times \text{LC} = 2
\mathrm{mm} + 45 \times 0.01
\mathrm{mm} = 2.45
\mathrm{mm}$.
Correct reading $= 2.45 - 0.04 = 2.41
\mathrm{mm} = 241 \times 10^{-2}
\mathrm{mm}$.
Therefore, $x = 241$.
